questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A country with a complete partnership (no tuition fee) and a university with an academically high ambition. 
Also, a country with great possibilities of exploring nature as well as urban life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy I would say. McGill gives no introduction to MyCourses though, which is the platform for all courses with reading materials. I'm lucky that other students introduced me to it. Otherwise, information was provided in emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly from other students in classes, but also a lot of emails from McGill.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just found it on AirBnB with three other exchange students. It was easy and a fair price (not cheap but also not expensive), and we all prioritized to have a place to stay when we arrived as opposed to finding a place when you arrive which can sometimes be cheaper.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is such an advantage to live close to the metro line that goes to McGill and Peel station. It takes no time to get to university and you feel connected to the city, even if you do not live in downtown.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only heard bad things about the student housing: that it is expensive and that there is a mandatory meal plan.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: An email account was created for me, so I only had to choose a password and then create a Minerva account. I had no problems with the registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure. I didn't need it so I didn't look into it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration process for courses was a mess. I did not like that it was open the first two weeks of the semester as it became a game for people to register for as many classes as possible. As an exchange student that had to take 400-level courses or up, it was really hard and took a lot of energy to get registered for the right courses (particularly as McGill did not open up 500-level courses for us).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a deep breath for the registration of classes! It will work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more classes than I'm used to at home so I spent more time at uni. There were many assignments and projects during the semester so I had to do some planning in order to make sure I could meet all of the deadlines. That said, I liked that it was ambitious.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: POLI 346, POLI 410, POLI 411 and POLI 445.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: POLI 346, POLI 410, POLI 411 and POLI 445. All the professors were very invested in teaching their courses and helpful if neededd.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: n.a.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everyday living expenses were more expensive than I was prepared for. I'm happy that I got grants to help cover the expenses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McGill gym is cheap and well-equipped. I also enjoyed the free use of the pool.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: McGill gym (for a small fee) and McGill pool (free).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: McGill gym (for a small fee) is well-equipped and McGill pool (free). Both are so easy to use between classes as it is located on campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Mont Royal, Mont Tremblant and just explore the city of Montréal.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and friendly. They will invite you in if you ask.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The one thing is that there is a more formal way of interacting with professors compared to my home university. Also, it is really an advantage with the locals if you do speak French to some level - they can speak English but they consider it polite if you start you by saying "salut" or "pardon". 
There are a lot of homeless people in the city which I personally had to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming nature of Canadians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be aware that there will be a lot of studying at McGill compared to what I've heard of at other universities. The academic level is ambitious and high, and there are a lot of assignments. But you do learn A LOT, and both students and professors are very good at helping.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: n.a.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning from the courses and getting to know local friends from uni (had classes with them).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Striking the right balance between being invested in the courses and learnings while also making time for extraordinary experiences such as weekend trips.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: n.a.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
